Salesforce Data: Record Cyber Week Expected to Deliver $75.8B in AI-Driven Sales
Retailers with shopper agents set to score big as consumers turn to AI and personal agents to find deals this holiday season
November 19, 2026
6 min read
Salesforce today predicts that the 2026 Cyber Week (Tuesday, November 24, through Monday, November 30) will drive a record $357 billion in global online sales, and $75.8 billion of that figure will be influenced by AI and agents, up 13% from 2025. AI-driven traffic to retailer sites is up 104% year over year, and AI-driven recommendations are expected to influence 1 in 5 holiday shopping orders.
Powered by aggregate data from Agentforce, Commerce Cloud, Service Cloud, and Marketing Cloud, these Cyber Week predictions are developed from
Salesforce’s Shopping Index
, which analyzes the real shopping activity of over 1.5 billion global shoppers across 1.5 trillion page views.
The index finds that global online sales this fall are up 5.5% from 2025, despite higher rates of consumer pessimism this year. As retailers begin the season with 5% higher discount rates, shoppers are not only spending more but also placing more orders and buying more at checkout than they did last year. And with nearly 70% of shoppers waiting for Cyber Week to make big purchases, Salesforce predicts a record kickoff to the holiday shopping season.
“We’re expecting a blockbuster Cyber Week despite economic headwinds,” said Caila Schwartz, Head of Agentic Commerce Shopper Insights at Salesforce. “This year, AI is playing a big role for both shoppers and retailers, from discovery to
checkout
. Consumers are turning to personal agents to discover gifts and find the best deals, and the brands ready to meet that demand with their own shopper
agents
will see the biggest returns this holiday season.”
Salesforce data finds
that both brands and shoppers are using AI to optimize the holiday shopping season. The Salesforce Consumer Shopping survey found that 31% of consumers have already tried a personal agent like Meta’s Muse or OpenAI’s Dots, and nearly 20% use AI tools as the first stop in their holiday shopping journey. Retailers with agents — like
SharkNinja
and Hibbett Sports — will see healthier holiday spending, as shoppers who engage with agents spend 8% more per order and build 23% bigger baskets. In fact, Salesforce predicts 1 in 3 retailers will have agents like
Carter, the Shopper Agent
, available on their site by Cyber Week.
“Personalization is our core focus this holiday season,” said Sarah Wangaard, SVP, Marketing, Hibbett Sports. “Hibbett AI, our Salesforce-powered shop agent, helps us do this at scale. It now handles 90% of core shopper journeys, guiding customers from product discovery all the way to purchase. Paired with
Agentforce Voice
, which handles order status, returns, and FAQs with a seamless handoff to a live team member, it helps us bring the personal, low-friction experience our customers love in our stores to every channel, even at peak volume.”
Salesforce’s Cyber Week 2026 Predictions
Cyber Week sales are expected to hit all time highs:
Cyber Week online sales are expected to reach
$357 billion
worldwide (up 6% year over year) and
$84 billion
in the U.S. (up 6% year over year).
Online sales are up this fall, with sales between October 1 and November 15 increasing 5% year over year in the U.S. and 5.5% globally.
AI will drive 21% of Cyber Week sales:
Salesforce anticipates that
$75.8 billion
, or
21%
of all global sales, will be influenced by
AI
and agents during Cyber Week. This is a significant increase from
$67 billion in 2025
.
AI-driven traffic to retailer websites is up
104%
year over year.
Twenty percent of holiday shopping traffic will be nonhuman.
Shoppers arriving via AI referrals are
two times
as likely to convert compared with typical ecommerce shoppers.
Consumers turn to AI and personal agents to kick off their shopping:
One in five shoppers will start their holiday shopping with AI — including personal agents — and
74%
of consumers trust the recommendations they get from AI.
One in three
shoppers are introduced to new brands through AI assistants, and
11%
say they won’t buy something if AI tells them not to.
Thirty-one percent
of consumers have already tried personal agents, and
8%
have had their agent make purchases for them.
The top use case for personal agents is price comparison, as budget-conscious shoppers look for deals.
But
73%
of shoppers still aren’t ready to hand over their credit card details to a personal agent.
Retailers with agents will see bigger orders:
One in three brands will have shopper agents on their websites by Cyber Week, and those brands will see boosts in holiday orders and customer loyalty.
Thirty-nine percent
of shoppers have used a brand’s shopper agent, and
80%
of them had a good experience. Of those shoppers,
75%
felt more loyal to the brand.
Shoppers who engage with a brand’s shopper agent spend
8%
more per order and purchase
23%
more items.
Brands that deploy shopper agents also see
seven times
faster sales growth than competitors that don’t offer agents.
Social media will dominate Cyber Week
: Social shopping will peak on the Tuesday and Wednesday before Thanksgiving, with 16% planning to shop inside social media platforms through the holidays.
Twenty-three percent
of ecommerce traffic is coming from clicks in social media channels, up
13%
year over year, led by increases from TikTok and Instagram.
The share of orders from social media referrals grew
27%
year over year across October and November.
Over
1 in 4
shoppers have made a purchase inside a social media app, such as TikTok Shop, in the past three months.
Tech-savvy Gen Z will shop in store:
In-store shopping remains the number one holiday shopping destination, with
71%
of shoppers planning to shop in store this holiday season.
One in three
Gen Z shoppers plan to visit a store for an early-morning Black Friday promotion.
Sixty-three percent
of Gen Z shoppers plan to shop in store this holiday season.
Retailers look to make holidays affordable amid economic headwinds:
Shoppers are seeing higher discounts than this time last year, with discount rates up
5%
globally and up
8%
in the U.S. in November.
The result is flat pricing compared with last holiday, with average selling prices for physical goods down
2%
year over year globally and down
1%
year over year in the U.S.
Retailer efforts to control pricing are enabling shoppers to build bigger baskets early in the season, with basket sizes up
3%
year over year globally and in the U.S.
Cyber Week is still the best time of year to find the steepest discounts:
Retailers are prepared to offer enticing deals to lure shoppers this Cyber Week.
Salesforce expects the highest discounted categories globally to be:
Beauty, makeup (
38%
)
General apparel (
33%
)
Beauty, skincare (
30%
)
It projects the highest discounted categories in the U.S. to be:
General apparel (
38%
)
Health and beauty (
33%
)
Home (furniture, dining, decor, appliances) (
23%
)
Explore further
Visit Salesforce’s
Shopping Insights HQ
for real-time Cyber Week results
Learn how
consumers are using personal agents
to get a jump on holiday shopping
Learn more about powering agentic shopping experiences with
Commerce Cloud
2026 Salesforce holiday insights and predictions methodology
Powered by Agentforce, Commerce Cloud, Service Cloud, and Marketing Cloud, Salesforce analyzed aggregated data to produce holiday insights from the activity of more than 1.5 billion global shoppers across more than 89 countries, with a focus on 18 key markets: the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Japan, the Netherlands, Australia, New Zealand, the Asia-Pacific (excluding Japan, Australia, and New Zealand), Switzerland, Latin America (LAM), the Middle East and Africa (MEA), Eastern Europe, Belgium, and the Nordics. This battery of benchmarks provides a deep look into the last nine quarters and the current state of digital commerce. Several factors are applied to extrapolate macroeconomic figures for the broader retail industry. These and other results are not indicative of Salesforce performance.
The prediction data that we present are from proprietary Salesforce research. The calculations we use blend together first-party and third-party data, as well as several market assumptions.

Salesforce to Lead Consortium Bringing Trusted American SI to Global Markets

Commerce designation supports Salesforce’s delivery of governed data, model choice, and agents that modernize government services and business operations
Media Library
SAN FRANCISCO and WASHINGTON, November 19, 2026
— Salesforce, the world’s #1 CRM, announced that the U.S. Department of Commerce has
selected
its consortium as one of 33 initial pre-set consortia offering designated priority Super Intelligence (SI) export packages under the
American SI Exports Program
. The initiative is designed to expand international markets for American technology and strengthen U.S. leadership in advanced technologies.
Through the program, Salesforce’s consortium package is included among designated American technology offerings that U.S. and Foreign Commercial Service representatives and interagency partners will offer to foreign buyers globally. The designation also makes Salesforce’s package eligible for priority government-to-government engagement, priority export control review, and priority routing for federal financing referrals.
Salesforce’s selection builds on more than two decades of experience supporting some of the world’s most complex government missions. Today, its technology supports government operations in more than 30 countries, including work with 60 U.S. federal agencies, all 15 U.S. Cabinet departments, and all 50 states.
“American technology leadership grows when governments and businesses around the world put it to work with trust,” said Kendall Collins, President and CEO of Missionforce and Government Cloud at Salesforce. “Salesforce brings governed data, enterprise applications, and agents together to deliver faster public services, stronger operations, and greater productivity—with model choice and controls that respect customers’ sovereignty. Through the American SI Exports Program, we’re bringing American innovation and deep operational expertise to help our global partners turn intelligence into action.”
Salesforce’s consortium offering puts that vision into practice with:
Trusted cloud infrastructure:
Hyperforce, Salesforce’s cloud architecture, runs on leading U.S. cloud infrastructure that supports local sovereignty and data residency needs.
Governed data:
Data 360 and Zero Copy partners provide governed data without duplicating it across systems, while Informatica strengthens data governance and quality.
AI models and security:
The Atlas Reasoning Engine helps AI agents reason and take action using
Salesforce xGen models
and leading third-party LLMs, with security controls from the Einstein Trust Layer and Salesforce Shield.
Enterprise applications:
Agentforce delivers pre-built agents for customer and constituent service, case management, and operations.
Together, these capabilities connect American innovation into real-world applications, helping public and private sector organizations modernize operations while maintaining control over their data, models, and deployment.

items.title: Informatica from Salesforce brings Trusted Enterprise Data into Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and Microsoft Fabric to Accelerate AI & Analytics
items.content:

Skip to Footer
0%
Salesforce Partners
Informatica from Salesforce brings Trusted Enterprise Data into Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and Microsoft Fabric to Accelerate AI & Analytics
November 17, 2026
7 min read
Expanded Microsoft collaboration brings Informatica’s enterprise data intelligence directly into Microsoft Copilot for business users and Microsoft Foundry for AI developers, while strengthening trusted analytics across Microsoft Fabric.
Announcement Highlights
Bringing Trusted Enterprise Data to Microsoft Copilot and Teams:
New integration extends Informatica’s enterprise data intelligence into Copilot & Teams, helping business users and executives access authoritative business definitions, data quality, governance, and lineage insights through natural-language experiences.
Powering Governed AI Agents in Microsoft Foundry:
Expanded integration with Informatica Headless introduces new Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based governance, identity, and administrative capabilities, enabling developers to build agents grounded in trusted data.
Expanding Trusted Governance for Microsoft Fabric:
Enhanced scanning and lineage capabilities now include notebooks and pipelines, providing greater visibility into how data moves and transforms across analytics workloads.
Expanding Deployment Choice on Microsoft Azure:
A new U.S. East Coast Azure point of delivery expands deployment choice for enterprises with regional data residency and compliance considerations.
Informatica
, a leader in AI-powered enterprise cloud data management, today announced an expanded collaboration with Microsoft at Microsoft Ignite 2026.
The collaboration introduces a Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Teams integration and expanded
data governance
capabilities for Microsoft Foundry and Microsoft Fabric. As enterprises move from AI experiments to agents performing business-critical work, those agents need more than access to data. They need to understand business definitions, identify authoritative sources, assess data quality, and operate within access policies.
According to Deloitte’s 2026
State of AI in the Enterprise
report
, 85% of organizations expect to customize
AI agents
for their business needs, but only 21% of organizations planning agentic AI deployments report having mature agent governance models.
Informatica addresses this challenge by bringing the intelligence embedded within its AI-ready Data Platform that includes enterprise business glossaries, metadata, lineage, data quality, master data, and governance directly into the AI experiences enterprises are adopting.
“The next frontier of enterprise AI isn’t simply giving every employee an intelligent assistant or every developer the ability to build agents. It’s ensuring that those assistants and agents understand the business they’re operating in.
With Informatica and Microsoft’s AI and Analytics experiences, we’re bringing trusted enterprise data directly to where people ask questions, make decisions, and build intelligent systems. Business users can benefit from the same authoritative data intelligence that developers use to build governed AI agents.
We’re making enterprise data management more accessible, more intelligent, and more relevant to every person and every agent across the organization.”
—
Savinay Berry, EVP & General Manager, Data Management, Salesforce
Bringing trusted enterprise data to Copilot
Informatica’s new integration with Copilot is designed to bridge that gap by making enterprise data intelligence accessible within the conversational AI experiences employees use to get work done. Through
Informatica Headless
capabilities, Copilot experiences are enriched with enterprise context drawn from Informatica’s data catalog, business glossary, metadata, lineage, quality indicators, and governance services.
This means business professionals can move beyond asking what information exists to understanding what that information actually means, where it originated, how trustworthy it is, and how it should be interpreted. Imagine a marketing manager using Copilot to create a campaign that targets a segment of customers for a new feature launch. To develop an effective campaign, the marketing manager needs to identify the most relevant and authoritative datasets, assess their quality, understand the data lineage and provenance, and ensure compliance with access control for sensitive information, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII). By bringing together these critical elements of enterprise data context through Informatica MCPs into the Copilot experience, the marketing manager (business user), can confidently design, execute and optimize campaigns using trusted, governed and AI-ready data.
Copilot brings AI to the business user. Informatica brings the enterprise’s trusted data intelligence to Copilot.
Extending Foundry with governed enterprise data for AI agents
While Copilot makes trusted context more accessible to business users, Foundry provides developers with the tools to build and deploy AI agents that can reason and act across enterprise systems.
Building on the general availability of Informatica Headless MCP servers in Foundry announced at Informatica World 2026, the expanded integration introduces new and updated governance, identity, and administrative capabilities.
These enhancements expand access to Informatica’s data management capabilities through standardized MCP interfaces and enable enterprise AI developers to:
Ground AI agents in trusted business data: Give agents access to authoritative definitions, quality indicators, and lineage so they can better understand and interpret enterprise information.
Govern agent access and actions: Apply identity, access, and administrative controls that help keep agent activity within established enterprise policies.
Enhanced governance and auditability: Administrative capabilities help customers control and trace agent interactions with enterprise data management services.
Accelerate enterprise AI development: Enable Foundry developers to discover and use Informatica’s data management capabilities through standardized MCP interfaces rather than building custom integrations.
Drive multicloud enterprise context: Informatica enables Foundry agents to benefit from governed data intelligence spanning systems and environments beyond Microsoft Azure.
By expanding the availability of Informatica’s MCP services across Azure-based IDMC points of delivery worldwide, more organizations can incorporate trusted enterprise data into Foundry applications and agents.
Deepening trusted analytics across Fabric
As enterprises increasingly adopt Fabric to unify their analytics environments, understanding how data moves and changes across complex workloads has become essential to maintaining trust. Informatica is extending its Fabric scanning capabilities to include notebooks and data pipelines, expanding governance visibility beyond data at rest to the orchestration and transformation processes that shape enterprise information.
The enhanced scanners provide broader lineage visibility across data movement and transformation workflows, including multistep pipeline orchestrations. These innovations help customers:
Expand end-to-end data lineage by tracing data movement and transformation across Fabric notebooks and pipelines.
Strengthen governance and impact analysis: Better understand dependencies and the implications of changes across Fabric environments.
Simplify administration: Manage Fabric scanning services through a consolidated interface, reducing operational complexity.
Enrich enterprise context for AI with lineage, provenance, and governance intelligence that can inform downstream AI experiences.
Deliver more reliable analytics and AI: Provide data engineers, analysts, and AI developers with greater confidence in the provenance, quality, and meaning of the data they consume.
As Informatica extends governance and lineage visibility across Fabric, the resulting metadata and trust signals enrich the enterprise context made available to AI agents through Copilot and Foundry.
“
As AI becomes part of everyday work, organizations need intelligent experiences that understand the business context behind their information. Microsoft Copilot helps people work more effectively, Microsoft Foundry enables developers to build powerful AI agents, and Microsoft Fabric serves as a primary data source fueling these experiences. Microsoft IQ brings these capabilities together with a shared intelligence layer that connects data and business context to help AI understand how an organization works. Our expanded collaboration with Informatica brings authoritative data definitions, quality, lineage, and governance into these experiences. By combining Microsoft’s AI innovation with Informatica’s enterprise data management, we’re helping customers make AI more relevant, more trustworthy, and easier to scale
.”
— Yitzhak Kessleman, Corporate Vice President, Microsoft IQ, Microsoft
Expanding Informatica’s Azure footprint to support enterprise choice
Informatica is also expanding its geographic footprint on Azure, with a new U.S. East Coast point of delivery. The new deployment option is designed for enterprises seeking to align cloud architecture, data residency preferences, and procurement requirements with U.S. East Coast–based infrastructure.
The new Azure pod offers Informatica’s broad portfolio of cloud data management services, including data integration, data governance, data quality, master data management, and agentic data management capabilities. Customers will also be able to benefit from advanced serverless integration capabilities available as an Azure Native ISV Service.
Customers can apply 100% of the pre-tax amount of Informatica offers, purchased through Microsoft Marketplace toward their Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment (MACC), subject to Microsoft’s eligibility requirements.
“
Integrating Informatica with Microsoft Foundry and Fabric is helping Wescom Financial close the gap between raw data and real AI readiness. We now have the contextual, trusted data layer our teams need to deploy AI with confidence — and that’s accelerating how quickly we can turn insight into action
.” —
Desigan Reddi, Vice President of Enterprise Architecture and Innovation, Wescom Financial
Related
Salesforce and Microsoft Announce Copilotforce, Bringing Salesforce Customer Context and Sales Workflows to Microsoft Copilot
7 min read
Why We Post-Trained Our Own Reasoning Model
6 min read
The next chapter of enterprise AI: Intelligence grounded in trusted data
The latest innovations build on the companies’ longstanding collaboration across Azure, Fabric, and Informatica’s AI-ready Data Platform.
For organizations investing in AI, the challenge is no longer simply connecting more data or deploying more sophisticated models. It is ensuring that every AI-powered decision and action is grounded in accurate, governed, and business-relevant information. As enterprises increasingly adopt AI agents, conversational assistants, and unified analytics platforms, the value of enterprise data management is expanding beyond traditional technical users.
Informatica’s enterprise-wide data management capabilities complement Microsoft’s AI development, semantic intelligence, and analytics platforms by providing an additional layer of authoritative data definitions, quality, lineage, and governance across hybrid and multicloud environments. For business leaders, that means greater confidence in AI-generated insights and decisions. For developers and data professionals, it means easier access to governed enterprise data management capabilities through the Microsoft tools they already use.
The future of enterprise AI isn’t just about making AI smarter. It’s about making AI understand the enterprise — and giving every employee and every agent the trusted data to act with confidence.

Microsoft Copilot integration: Generally available.
Microsoft Foundry: Informatica Headless MCP server integration is generally available, with expanded governance, identity, and administration.
Microsoft Fabric Scanners from Informatica: General Availability of expanded scanning capabilities for notebooks and pipelines along with consolidated Informatica scanner administration.
Azure U.S. East IDMC point of delivery: Generally available
